properties.title: PA Permit Violation Issued to TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC in Sugar Grove Township, Warren County
properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 6/08/2026 to TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC in Sugar Grove Township, Warren county. 91.33(A) - INCIDENTS CAUSING OR THREATENING POLLUTION - Failure to notify the Department of an accident or other activity or incident, a toxic substance or another substance which would endanger downstream users of the waters, result in pollution or create a danger of pollution of the waters of this Commonwealth, or would damage property.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/08/2026
Violation Code: 91.33(A) - INCIDENTS CAUSING OR THREATENING POLLUTION - Failure to notify the Department of an accident or other activity or incident, a toxic substance or another substance which would endanger downstream users of the waters, result in pollution or create a danger of pollution of the waters of this Commonwealth, or would damage property.
Violation ID: 8277567
Permit API: 123-47222
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Sugar Grove Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 6/08/2026
Comments: A discharge of production fluids is evident at the Loomis Lease tank battery. Elevated specific conductance in soils was observed beneath one of the stock tank's drain valves within the secondary containment area as well as throughout a swath of stressed and dead vegetation downslope of the Loomis Lease tank battery. Brian Ayers (WQSS-DEP) and I (Mat Haemer WQS-DEP) were present for this inspection.Evidence of a concentrated flow of fluids was observed just beyond the secondary containment diking. Bare soils outside of containment were observed to have been eroded in a manner consistent with the channelized flow of a large volume of fluid. The bottom of the eroded channel was found to have elevated specific conductance in excess of 2,000 micro Siemens per centimeter.Areas downslope of the tank battery where the flow of fluid was observed to widen (visible via the wide swath of stressed and dead vegetation) were observed to have elevated specific conductance in soils in excess of 5,000 micro Siemens per centimeter.The downslope path of the released fluid was then captured by a lease road ditch approximately 150 feet downslope of the tank battery. Observations of elevated specific conductance in soils within the road ditch continued to a culvert nearby to the Loomis Lease Loomis 3 OG well. Standing water at the outflow of this culvert was found to have elevated specific conductance in excess of 1,300 micro Siemens per centimeter. Elevated soil conductivity readings in excess of 1,000 micro Siemens per centimeter continued for approximately 100 feet from the outfall of the culvert.The total observed path of stressed/dead vegetation and elevated conductivity readings was approximately 750 feet in length and up to 30 feet in width. Because the volume of this release exceeds the 1 bbl threshold, the use of either the Act 2 or Alternative Remediation Process is required.It is requested that Trinity Mineral Partners provide the Department with receipts documenting the proper disposal of brine resulting from producing the Loomis Lease.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: ARD OPR LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/22/2021
Violation Code: 78a57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect brine and other fluids produced during operation of the well in a tank, series of tanks, or other device approved by the Department for subsequent disposal or reuse.
Violation ID: 911115
Permit API: 081-21802
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Cascade Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 3/22/2021
Comments: An incident inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator that produced water was released from a GPU dump line. The report stated that on Saturday, March 20, 2021, a crew monitoring the wells remotely noticed erratic gauge trends and the volume of the release was initially estimated at 1 to 5 barrels in this notification. I met with ARD representative Rick Hall on location. Mr. Hall told me that a failed valve on the 10H well GPU led to a release of 12 barrels of produced water to the pad surface. He said that they believe that the GPU dump line sprayed produced water inside the double-walled GPU for 2 hours and since the well produces an average of 12 barrels of produced water per hour, the total volume released from the line was 24 barrels. The containment within the GPU held 12 barrels of produced water and 12 barrels overflowed to the pad surface. The 10H well was remotely shut-in after two hours of erratic gauge trends. Mr. Hall stated that ARD intends to pursue Act 2 remediation and they contracted an environmental consultant, GES, to oversee the process. A line of puddles is present along the west edge of the pad. The electrical conductivity (EC) of these puddles is 8.35 mS/cm in the area closest to the 10H GPU and the EC in the puddles decreases steadily farther away. The GPU was moved to another area of the pad and in the small puddle on the pad where it had been staged, the EC was greater than 19.99 mS/cm. When I relayed my findings to Mr. Hall, he stated that on Saturday morning, the puddles along the west side of the pad were all below 1 mS/cm. I took a sample, ID# 0718-175, from the puddle along the west side of the pad where the EC is between 7.5 and 8.35 mS/cm, adjacent to the location where the 10H GPU had been staged. The sample was sent to the state laboratory on the same day to be analyzed for SAC 942 plus Br, Li, and Al. The Department recommends pursuing Act 2 remediation. Violations noted.

SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP.  Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.

Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 1/10/2023
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 981231
Permit API: 105-21923
Unconventional: Yes
County: Potter
Municipality: Ulysses Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 1/10/2023
Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an INCIDENT inspection of the JKLM - Headwaters 146 Well Pad located in Ulysses Twp, Potter Co. on 1/10/23 @1045 hours in response to report of a release of 32 gallons of produced fluid from a dehydration unit. The weather was 31 degrees, cloudy, winds WNW @5mph. Activity onsite consists of AES and JKLM personnel bringing Gas Production Equipment back online after the reported release. On 1/9/23 Joe Herrick of JKLM called to report that at 9:45 a.m., a lever control malfunctioned on their 2HU GPU unit and sent a slug of produced water to their dehydration unit resulting in a misting of produced water and a little glycol throughout the exhaust of the dehydration unit. They are estimating about 32 gallons was released. Onsite JKLM personnel estimated the impacted area to be approximately 35' x 25'. Personnel stated before cleanup began elevated conductivity readings of the pad surface were >19.99mS/cm in the immediate vicinity of the dehydration unit and fell to approximately 2-5mS/cm towards the periphery of the impacted area. Onsite Personnel stated the dehydration unit was washed down and fluid was recovered from the secondary containment. Pad material was removed from the impacted area and placed in 2 roll-off containers for disposal. The drains to the perimeter controls remain shut-in and perimeter controls were not impacted. As of today's inspection, the spill area appears to have been backfilled with clean material. Personnel were working onsite to get filters changed in the dehydration unit and get the GPU back online. No areas of elevated conductivity were observed. The spill area appeared adequately remediated.Violations of the following regulations are cited as IMMEDIATELY CORRECTED against the 2HU well API#105-21923:CSL 402(b)SWMA 30125 Pa Code 78a.57(a)I departed the site at 1350 hours.

Report Details

Violation Code: 78a57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect brine and other fluids produced during operation of the well in a tank, series of tanks, or other device approved by the Department for subsequent disposal or reuse.
Violation ID: 8268740
Permit API: 059-26446
Unconventional: Yes
County: Greene
Municipality: Washington Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 3/27/2026
Comments: On 03/27/2026, an incident inspection was conducted at the Anthony Petraitis Well Site following receipt of a spill report, submitted to the Department on 03/26/2026 (CTS 396174). I was accompanied by Water Quality Specialist Laura Grada (PA DEP), EQT representative Doug Oberdorf, and SPSI representative Billy Wade. SPSI was on site for remediation.EQT reported a spill of approximately 5 gallons of production fluid from a flow line. They reported that SPSI was on site, the release was contained, and no waterways were affected.EQT indicated on site that they intend to remediate per Act 2 guidelines. The fluid was on the pad, underneath the pad liner; the pad liner was above the pad substrate and contained pea gravel overtop of the liner. When the Department arrived on site, SPSI indicated that 1 vac box was around half full of the removed fluids; this was the only box that was used, and none were removed from site full.The following was observed during inspection:SPSI had vac trucks on site and were in the process of remediation (Photo 1).The spill was located around Gas Production Unit (GPU) 6H. The leak originated at the elbow joint of the associated GPU piping. The spilled fluid reached the underside of the pad liner; the fluid was also pooling on top of the pad liner, within the pea gravel (Photos 2-5).Several sumps were dug on both sides of the spill origin at GPU 6H and its associated elbow joint within the piping. Conductivity readings were obtained within the soil and water at the sump locations. The sump located 15 feet from the elbow joint yielded a conductivity reading of 1835 uS/cm within the soil (Photo 6). The sump 30 feet from the elbow joint yielded a conductivity reading of 644 uS/cm within the soil (Photo 7). The sump located 10 feet from the elbow yielded a water conductivity reading of 13.04 mS/cm and a soil reading of 6.18 mS/cm (Photos 8, 9). The sump located 35 feet from the elbow yielded a conductivity reading of 2.86 mS/cm within the soil this reading was unable to be replicated; the operator will monitor this location (Photo 10). The sump located 20 feet from the elbow yielded a conductivity reading of 176.2 uS/cm within the water, and a reading of 2.83 mS/cm within the soil (Photos 11, 12).The large sump, to the left of GPU 6H, yielded a conductivity reading of 1660 uS/cm within the water, and a reading of 2.48 mS/cm within the soil (Photos 13-15). The large sump, to the right of GPU 6H, yielded a conductivity reading of 397 uS/cm within the water, and a reading of 8.26 mS/cm within the soil (Photos 16-18).The soil within the impacted area yielded a reading of 13.39 mS/cm (Photo 19). The water on the liner yielded a conductivity reading that was Over Range (>20.00 mS/cm) (Photo 20).The soil adjacent to the sump behind GPU 6H yielded a conductivity reading of 670 uS/cm; the soil within the sump yielded a reading of 7.55 mS/cm, and the water within this sump yielded a reading of 1450 uS/cm (Photos 21-23).The pooled water and soil on the far side of the berm, behind GPU 6H, did not display elevated conductivity (Photo 24).The Act 9 sign was at the site entrance. The Emergency Response Plan was on site. A QR code was available and displayed a large list of materials located on well sites. The information did not appear to be site specific (Photo 25).Due to the release of production fluid, violations of 78a54, SWMA 301, 78a57(a), and 91.34(a) are being issued.

Comments: On 4/29/26, DEP performed a post plugging inspection of the Bookshar 2 (051-23037) in response to the operator submitting a certificate of well plugging "COWP" on 4/24/26. According to the COWP, the well was plugged on 3/31/26. The COWP was submitted within 30 days consistent with 78.124. The COWP was reviewed as part of this inspection report. properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/15/2023
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 988795
Permit API: 081-21881
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/15/2023
Comments: A follow-up inspection was conducted in order to assess conditions after multiple produced fluid releases on Pad B as well as sediment discharges from the access road. Both pads and the access road were snow-covered during this inspection. On Pad B, the production equipment is still being installed the flow lines from the well heads to the production equipment. The electrical conductivity (EC) in the trench near the B-11H well head was 2.1 mS/cm. The EC of the puddles in the northeast corner of Pad B where the MASS was located is 575 uS/cm. The EC of the fluid is 2.09 mS/cm in the sump at the east outlet of the north stormwater channel. The fluid flowing out of the east outlet of the stormwater channel had an EC of 1.4 mS/cm. In the northcentral area of the well pad, the excavated trenches are still present. The EC of the fluid in the largest trench near the north stormwater channel was 1.4 mS/cm. The fluid in the excavated portion of the north stormwater channel had an EC of 2.02 mS/cm.The east side of the well pad was being back-filled with gravel during this inspection. The berm of the secondary containment for the frac tank on the east side of the well pad is damaged.On Pad A, six wells are staged for production. Six GPUs are present within secondary containment. A battery of frac tanks are present within secondary.Violations remain outstanding against the ESCGP for the sediment discharges along the access road into the waters of the commonwealth.Violations remain outstanding for the reported produced fluid release from the MASS on Pad B from 12/19/22 against permit 081-21881.Violations remain outstanding against permit 081-21879 for the reported release of produced fluid from clam shell boxes in the northwest area of Pad B, in the area of the dancefloor, from 2/6/23.Violations remain outstanding against permit 081-21880 for the reported discovery of additional fluid with elevated electrical conductivity in the northcentral area of the pad in the area of the Sand X boxes.

properties.content:

Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 995063
Permit API: 053-29645
Unconventional: No
County: Forest
Municipality: Howe Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/15/2023
Comments: This conventional well is equipped with a pump jack. The well's operator information and API number are displayed on the jack.There is an approximate 1' x 10' area of oil soaked soil on the ground next to the well from repeated venting of this well and its associated discharge of production fluids.A tank battery located 100 feet northeast of this well consists of two 210 bbl stock tanks inside of an earthen diking. There is evidence of production fluid releases onto the gravel inside of the diking given staining of the gravel and elevated specific conductance (SPC) within the stained areas. In addition to the issues inside of the diking, there is upwards of a barrel of crude oil/production fluids outside of the northern diking wall. Two sizable pools of crude oil are present within approximately 25' of the diking, while soil with elevated SPC and an abundance of deer tracks are present across the forest floor for another 25 feet to the north.It is requested that documentation of production water disposal from this lease be provided to the Department. Please see the attached Notice of Violation regarding requested information pertaining to the cause of the release and intentions to remediate the contaminated material within and outside of the tank battery.

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Date: 8/16/2021
Comments: This inspection report has been developed to document an on-site routine complete inspect, and to summarize the overall status of this well and well location. The project was recently acquired by Big Dog Energy, LLC. Applications for the transfer of all five wells permitted on the site, from Geopetro LLC to Big Dog Energy LLC, were received by the Department on August 2, 2021. An application for the transfer of the ESCGP that is currently active on the site was also received by the Department. The current Operator information has not yet been updated in the Department's electronic database. Well number 019-21928, along with four other wells, (API ID#'s: 019-21907, 019-21929, 019-21931, 019-21932), were drilled and currently exist on the location. Although the Act Nine sign has been changed to reflect the current owner of the well location, the well tags have not yet been updated. Updated well tags should be installed on each of the wells at some point in the near future. Inspection ID number's 2139667, 2139736, 2139741, 2199744 and 2139746, (conducted on February 13, 2013), suggests that all of the wells have been stimulated. Subsequent inspections indicate that that the wells have been on inactive status since at least March of 2014. ESCGP number ESX11-019-0091 is currently active on the site. The permit was renewed by RE Gas in 2017 and is set to expire on 09/15/2022. None of the earthwork proposed in the plan was ever implemented in the field. The location consists of one very large well location and a separate tank pad. The location is overgrown and clearly has not been tended to in any way for some time. There are currently, however, no clear E&S or stabilization-related issues associated with the site.

Comments: On location to witness the conclusion of 72-hr (Stepped) pressure build-up tests, (SPBUT) being performed on all (3) wells on the Susan pad. The Susan 2H, 4H and the 5H wells. These tests are being performed to assess the results of the initial remedial deployment of Renegades localized casing expansion tool in the production casing of the Susan 4H and 5H completed on 5/26/2021. SPBUTs were initiated on 3/14/22 @ ~ 10:00 and progressed by shutting in the outer most annuli of each well for first 24-hrs, then in 24-hr progressions, sequentially shutting in the next inner annuli, resulting in a total 72-hr SPBUT. - All (3) wells annuli are shut in. - Upon arrival I met with CALLC Field Rep. Craig Shores and Creston Consultant Reps., Will Dolan and Jason Rajan. Starting at approx. 10:00am, ending annuli pressures were checked using a Digital Crystal gauge. Gas checks were performed by Creston Reps., using a Bascom Turner Gas Explorer meter. Creston Consultants collected gas samples off annuli, where present, and will send out for isotopic analysis. CALLC will share gas sample results with The Department when received. Comments: Site inspection at COP Tract 231 Pad A on August 28, 2020 with Rick Hall of ARD in regards to the spill reported earlier that morning. Prior to my arrival Mr. Hall was able to take some photos prior to the rain arriving. Mr. Hall's photos have been included in this inspection report. According to lease hand operator Matt Coppadge of ARD, he was manually dumping water from the dehydration unit to the produced fluids tanks via the 2" buried steel line. When Mr. Coppadge pressured back-up, he observed dust in the air and a wet spot on the surface of the well pad. He immediately stop pressurizing the line. When he assessed the well pad, he observed two holes on the surface of the well pad and a wet spot ~6-8 ft. in diameter. The release was later reported to the Department by Mr. Hall.When I arrived onsite, the well pad was wet due to the rain. Mr. Hall marked off impacted areas on the surface of the well pad based off soil screenings using a soil conductivity probe. I viewed the impacted area where the released had occurred. I screened the area using a soil probe. Soils/gravel right at the two holes on the well pad exceeded the meters range of 4.00 mS/cm. As I moved away from the holes, readings decreased. Elevated soil readings were in an area approximate 6-8 ft. in diameter. An oil sheen was observed on the well pad near the holes and in a nearby puddle of water. The contractor arrived onsite the same time I did. In addition, Matt Lock of Tuscarora Geologic & Environmental Services arrived onsite prior to my departure. Mr. Lock will be collecting samples on behalf of ARD. Please note that is 2" buried steel dump line serves all three producing Marcellus wells located on this well pad. ARD is currently unable to determine the amount of produced fluids released. Due to the unknown volume of the release, the site is required to be remediated under 78a.66 through the Act 2 process.Violations noted. - Invalid Complaint Id. - 35148

Comments: On 6/9/2026, a representative from the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident response inspection (CTS #: 398384) of STL Resources LLCs Kjelgaard 802 multi-well pad located in Gaines Township, Tioga County. Upon arrival to the site at 0915 hours, weather was 72F and partly cloudy. An Act 9 sign is visible and located at the site entrance (photo #1).No fluids were observed on the pad surface field.This inspection was conducted in response to a release of approximately 15 gallons of produced fluids onto the pad surface from a pressure relief valve on 6/8/2026 at 1100 hours, STL immediately reported this incident to the DEP (photo #2). Upon arrival to the site, the impacted pad material had already been scraped and removed from the site and hauled to WM Phoenix Resources Landfill in Wellsboro for disposal. I screened soils in this area for electrical conductivity which ranged from ~130-500us/cm.There are 3 wells tagged with American Petroleum Institute (API) numbers located onsite, a workover rig was also observed performing well maintenance (photos #7 and 8). 3 gas processing units (GPUs) are also located onsite (photo #9). The GPUs do not utilize any visible secondary containment structures. A steel double-walled produced fluids tank is located onsite (photo #10); this tank utilizes an integrated secondary containment structure. A temporary storage tank was observed onsite and is currently in use for well maintenance activities (photo #11). The area surrounding the site remains permanently stabilized with greater than 70% uniform perennial vegetative cover. No accelerated erosion or sedimentation was observed. No post construction stormwater management (PCSM) controls are installed onsite.Based on the findings of this inspection, the following violations are noted against API #: 117-20185 and have been immediately corrected due to STL Resources immediate remediation and removal of the impacted pad material:-25 PA 78a.57(a)-35 P.S. 691.402(b)-35 P.S. 6018.301No additional violations noted. I departed the site at 1015 hours.

Comments: I arrived onsite at 1305 to conduct a routine complete inspection of the Corbin Well Pad.The inspection consisted of checking the mailbox for required documents, inspecting all areas of the site for E and S/stabilization issues, and a cursory inspection of the production equipment for any obvious issues. The site's ESCGP expired in 2022 but PCSM stormwater control measures (SCMs ) were never installed. As a result, the permit is still active and has not been terminated. Violations were noted in the most recent inspection of the site (SAIR #4168712). In a written response to that inspection, the operator stated that they had encountered several roadblocks when attempting to implement the PCSM plan. These include the identification of new wetlands where they had planned to place the proposed SCMs and the landowners request that they do not cut down any more trees within the LOD. These two issues reportedly restricted where the operator could place new SCMs. They stated that, as a result of the restrictions these two issues present, the site will have to be re-permitted. They estimated that the new permit package will be submitted in Fall 2026 with construction to begin shortly thereafter if weather permits. As of the date of inspection, no permit package has been received. Please see photos/findings for additional details regarding observations made during the inspection.Continuing violations noted.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 8/17/2022 to CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC in Wyalusing Twp, Bradford county. 78a57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect  brine and other fluids produced during operation of the well in a tank, series of tanks, or other device approved by the Department for subsequent disposal or reuse.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 8/17/2022
Violation Code: 78a57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect brine and other fluids produced during operation of the well in a tank, series of tanks, or other device approved by the Department for subsequent disposal or reuse.
Violation ID: 965519
Permit API: 015-23540
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Wyalusing Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 8/17/2022
Comments: On 8/17/2022, DEP representative John Rogers conducted an incident inspection in response to a spill at the Chesapeake MTL well site. The spill Complaint ID 366296 was received by the department on 8/17/2022. It was 75 degrees and overcast when I arrived on location. The spill was reported as an estimated 40 gallons of produced water released to the ground due to a dump line failure on the produced water tank. The initial impacted area was reported as 5'x5'. When I arrived on location, i viewed the area around the production tank. A flow back tank was nearby, a vacuum truck was being set up near the production tank and a man lift was next to the tank. I witnessed orange paint on the ground enclosing an estimated 6'x8' foot area on the north side of the tank with dark-stained ground and enclosing an estimated 20'x20' area on the south side of the tank with lighter stained ground.I met Chesapeake's production manager Gordon Fleming. He said that he did not know the specifics of the spill but that the four wells were shut in and a crew was on site to vacuum the liquids and solids out of the production tank. The tank was going to be moved to a temporary location so the spill area, including the area under the tank, could be excavated. Gordon said that the flowback tank was going to be used for production fluids while the equipment and area associated with the spill were excavated, cleaned, repaired, and put back into service. While the vac truck crew was setting up, I viewed the contaminated area. I field tested the soil in the area marked off on the north side of the tank for conductivity with results of 1,720 uS next to the north side of the tank, 718 uS 6 feet to the northwest and 4 uS 5 feet to the northeast. Gordon put me in contact with Chesapeake's Environmental Representative Danielle Schaad who reported the following: The spill was witnessed by the lease operator who was in the process of stimulating the wells and was unloading fluids from the wells to the production tank. The piping above the tank washed out, causing the release. After reporting the spill, Chesapeake brought a drone to location to observe the area around the production tank from the air in order to visibly determine the extent of the spill. The orange paint on the ground marked the visual extent of the contamination. After the vac crew cleans the tank, it will be moved to the side, away from the contaminated area. Creston Environmental is being mobilized to the site and expected to start testing and excavating the contaminated area on 8/18/2022 at 8:00 hrs. Danielle said that Chesapeake was holding with the 40-gallon estimation of the spill until Creston Environmental is able to determine the extent of contamination and give a better estimation. The release of production fluid to the unprotected pad surface constitutes a violation of Section 402 of the Clean Streams Law, of 78A57(a) for improper control, storage and disposal of production fluids and SWMA 301 for improper management of residual waste. The department also recommends pursuing Act 2 remediation in accordance with 78a.66 due to the extent of the contamination and the estimation being close to the 42-gallon action level.I left the site at 16:10 hrs.On 8/18/2022 at 14:30 I arrived back at location to view the progress with the excavation. During the visit, I took pictures 14-21.I met with Danielle Schaad and with Creston Environmental Andrew Steffe. The excavated area was 35'x16'x2' and field tested at 995 uS conductance or less. Samples for laboratory testing were collected. Danielle did report that Chesapeake would pursue Act 2 Remediation. I did witness the excavated material piled up on plastic secondary containment. I did request a copy of the manifest upon disposal. As I was leaving the site, the excavated area was being filled in with clean material.
